newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Zenith resumes PC manufacturing.
newsitem.headline: India's Zenith resumes PC manufacturing.

text.p: India's Zenith Computers Ltd said on Thursday it planned to resume making personal computers in India following a cut in customs duty on computer components.

The company announced the plans in a statement one day after Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said customs duty on hard-disk drives, floppy disk drives and Compact Disc-Read Only Memory (CD-ROM) drives was being cut to 10 percent from 20 percent.
Zenith chairman Raj Saraf said in the statement that the reduction "has made PC (personal computer) manufacturing viable again".

Earlier Zenith had stopped production because it was more profitable to import personal computers and resell them. The duty on imported personal computers last month was 20 percent, the same as the duty on components.
"Manufacturing did not make sense then," Saraf said, adding that the reduction in customs duty had "shifted the balance back to indigenous manufacturing".
The Zenith chairman said a rough estimate showed that with the duty reduction, indigenous manufacture was now about five percent more competitive than importing computers.
The company said it was the fourth largest personal computer vendor in India and had turnover of 1.2 billion rupees last year.
Last year it sold about 25,000 personal computers in a total market of 365,000. It has manufacturing facilities in Goa and Mumbai.
